This implies that the pathophysiological mechanism underlying Purpura Fulminans may involve a dependency on anticoagulant agents, with Dalteparin potentially acting through a similar mechanism to Heparin, Bovine, or Parnaparin. The recurring indication of Purpura Fulminans as a condition requiring anticoagulant therapy supports the hypothesis that Dalteparin may be repurposed for the treatment of Acquired Purpura Fulminans, likely due to its anticoagulant properties. The evidence is consistent across multiple paths, reinforcing the notion that Dalteparin's use in Purpura Fulminans may have a direct or indirect role in the development of Acquired Purpura Fulminans.
